info.description:
**Pramaan** — *Don't claim it. Prove it.*

A registry of notable people in India where every claim carries evidence and every
certificate is cryptographically signed and publicly verifiable.

* **Public (no key):** directory, profiles, certificate verification, transparency log.
* **Authenticated:** sign in for a JWT, or create an API key (`pk_live_…`) and send it as
  `X-API-Key` or `Authorization: Bearer`. Keys carry scopes and a rate limit.
info.title: Pramaan API

get.description: RFC 8414 metadata. The authorization endpoint is the consent screen in the web app.
Anyone can verify a certificate offline using this Ed25519 public key.

Every agent run with its model usage: calls, tokens, latency and errors (from the llm_calls table), plus how many
events it produced. Tokens are reported, not priced: confirm the current price list before turning them into cost.
Abuse view (API-10): the busiest and most-throttled keys of the last few days. Counts and key names only; no owner contact details.

post.description: The human approval. Only a change that passed the guard AND the sandbox can be applied.
Turn a sentence into a field definition. Nothing is created until you POST /v1/admin/fields.
Shilpkar drafts an expand-only migration; it is linted and rehearsed on a scratch database. Passing makes it READY for two approvals; nothing is applied.
Four eyes: two DIFFERENT people must approve a migration that passed its checks. Approval does not run it; it produces a release note for a person.

get.description:
How people actually decided past escalated cases, and what a lower auto-approve threshold would have done to them. A report only: it
changes no setting (the threshold is governed and four-eyes) and decides nothing (I-1).

post.description: Revoking a certificate is public and permanent for that code, so it needs two people.

A reviewer says a confirmed claim looks wrong: the dispute graph re-fetches evidence, re-checks the claim and sends it to a person.
You cannot dispute a claim on your own profile (I-10). The key makes a double click a no-op.

Manual override of a claim's verification. Lowering a claim (back to self-claimed) is always immediate: it is the safe
direction. Raising it to 'confirmed by a reviewer' needs a second person when the governed setting claim_override_four_eyes is on.

202.description: Filed for a second person's approval

get.description: What the person agreed to, and when. Read-only: consent is changed by the person, never by staff.

get.description:
Other people with this name on Wikidata, beside the item the applicant confirmed is them, so a reviewer can tell who might be
mistaken for whom. Read-only; it is the same public lookup the applicant saw.

post.description: Close a review item without changing the profile's published status (used for document / requested reviews).
Safety switches change only through a four-eyes approval (and with a fresh MFA code).
Granting a role is a four-eyes action: this files the request; a second person approves it.

What the running server is really doing. Admin-only (the public /healthz reveals nothing).

post.description: Shilpkar drafts a view spec. It is validated and saved as a DRAFT (public to no one); a second person publishes it.

put.description: Save a new version of the spec. A draft is replaced in place. A published view keeps serving its live version until a second person publishes this one.

post.description: Make the draft live. Never the person who proposed or last edited it: two people look at every view before the public can.

get.description:
A recorded REAL verification run, for the public Agent Floor (spec 6.7). Safe by construction: only runs on profiles flagged as
fictional demos are ever eligible, so no real person's name or evidence can appear; the payload carries no profile, user or owner
identifier; and times are offsets from the start of the run. With no demo run on record it says so instead of falling back to a real one.

post.description: Ends the session and revokes every token issued so far (signs out on all devices).
Start (or restart, before confirming) enrolment: returns the secret and an otpauth:// link to scan. Shown once.
Lost your authenticator? A recovery code works once, in place of a 6-digit code, for the step-up window.
A new set (the old ones stop working). Needs a fresh step-up, so a stolen session cannot mint its own backdoor.
Prove you are present: unlocks sensitive staff actions for a few minutes.
Email a 6-digit code to the account's address; proves the applicant controls it.
